os_boot_complete.answer: t4 = systemd ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic of cloud-final.service, plus /proc/stat btime, read on the node by coldstart-agent.sh. NOT systemd-analyze.
os_boot_complete.implication: d34 (EC2 running -> t4) ends when cloud-final STARTS. The ParallelCluster cookbook (Chef/Cinc) runs inside cloud-final, so it falls in d45, not d34. No double counting and no recomputation needed.
os_boot_complete.systemd_analyze_use: run once, as a diagnostic on parked job 14 (notes/2026-09-19-compute-node-boot-anatomy.md). It gives multi-user.target = 3m20s, which includes cloud-final/Chef. It was never used as t4.
caveats: btime is integer seconds, so t4 is accurate to about 1 s
d34 also includes the hypervisor/firmware time between EC2 'running' and kernel start

gaps: cross-host comparisons (poller/CloudTrail/EventBridge on one side, node agent on the other) therefore rest on the AL2023 default chrony config, not on a measurement
chrony.indirect_check: Across all 113 cold rows, head-node poller t5 minus node-agent slurmd_active (node clock) = +0.38 to +2.08 s, median +1.09 s. It is always positive, which fits slurmd startup plus the registration RPC plus the 1 s poll. A node clock running ahead by more than ~0.4 s would push some rows negative. So this bounds skew loosely; it does not measure it.

t0_source.summary: No cell got t0 from Slurm accounting. There is no slurmdbd (AccountingStorageType=(null)), and `sacct` failed for every job (15 'command failed: sacct' warnings in phase4-remaining.log). pilot-c7i-4n and warm-c7i-1n got t0 from `scontrol show job -o` EligibleTime, through the poller's fallback. pilot-c7i-1n ran before that fallback existed, so merge.py synthesized t0 from the squeue submit time. In all three cells t0 is the Slurm submit time truncated to whole seconds (EligibleTime == SubmitTime for every scontrol record).

pilot-c7i-1n.command: squeue -h -o '%i|%T|%r|%D|%N|%V|%S'  (poller, every 1 s while the job is in squeue)
pilot-c7i-1n.field: %V = SubmitTime -> job_state.submit in poller.jsonl -> merge.py sets eligible := submit
pilot-c7i-1n.why_flagged: poller.jsonl has 0 job_acct events. The scontrol fallback was written after this cell finished (job 13 ended 23:02:34Z) and before pilot-c7i-4n started (23:39:10Z); see the Kiro session 2026-09-19 and the 09-20 checkpoint caveat

pilot-c7i-4n.command: sacct -P -n -X -o JobID,Submit,Eligible,Start,End,State,NNodes,NodeList -j <id>  -> fails (no slurmdbd)  -> scontrol show job <id> -o
pilot-c7i-4n.fetched: by the poller 5 s or more after the job leaves squeue, inside MinJobAge=300 s. 10/10 jobs have a job_acct record
pilot-c7i-4n.note: not flagged, but it is still not accounting data: job_acct events are written with source='poller' whether they came from sacct or scontrol, and sacct never succeeded

warm-c7i-1n.command: same as pilot-c7i-4n (sacct fails -> scontrol show job -o)

vs_slurmctld_submit.definition: t0 minus the timestamp on the slurmctld.log line '_slurm_rpc_submit_batch_job: JobId=<id>' (millisecond resolution)
vs_slurmctld_submit.interpretation: Every difference falls in (-1, 0], which is exactly what truncating to whole seconds produces. That confirms t0 is the submit time parsed in the right timezone, with no offset. Effect: t0 is about 0.5 s early on average (at most 1 s), so d01 and total are overstated by about 0.5 s. 'Eligible' here equals submit: none of these jobs had dependencies or --begin.
